U2 and their team reportedly approached the NFL themselves with the idea of doing a halftime show — obviously timed to capitalize not just on families gathered around the TV before a holiday, but, from U2's perspective, following closely on the heels of the Nov. 13 release of "Carnaval de Luz," the band's first album of new material in nine years. The album debuted at No. 4 on the latest Billboard 200 chart.

It was U2's third tango with the NFL, albeit its first in two decades. The Irish band famously did the Super Bowl halftime show in 2002, with an emphasis on honoring the victims of 9/11. In 2006, the group performed in celebration of the opening of the Louisiana Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

The group has kept up a heavy cycle of broadcast and streaming promotions before and since the new album release, including a surprise opening to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony at L.A.'s Peacock Theatre on Nov. 14, which is being edited into a special to be broadcast Dec. 8 on ABC.

articles.title: GTA 6 Players Report The Game Is Bricking Their PS5 Consoles & The Fixes Are Not Ideal
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a demanding title. If GTA 6's file size were any indication, PS5 and Xbox Series X/S were always in for a workout. Now, players are reporting that their PS5 consoles are crashing, allegedly due to the strain of long hours playing GTA 6. One Reddit user shares that after playing GTA […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Grand Theft Auto 6 is a demanding title. If GTA 6's file size were any indication, PS5 and Xbox Series X/S were always in for a workout. Now, players are reporting that their PS5 consoles are crashing, allegedly due to the strain of long hours playing GTA 6. One Reddit user shares that after playing GTA 6 for "about 20 hours or so," the game randomly crashed. And while this has been a recurring problem for many, this singular crash has seemingly affected the entirety of this particular Reddit user's system. "I am aware this is a known issue for people as of now, but now every game I have doesn't boot up for more than a minute before crashing, even small games that take barely any power."

The user also noted that upon startup, the console displays "glitchy patches" on the screen for a few seconds. This is far from the only case of this occurring. One streamer faced a similar issue while playing the game live.

#GTA6 tonight fried my PS5. The GPU is done and the console is gone 🫩 rip pic.twitter.com/KhLf62Ql8W

Even streams such as xQc and iShowSpeed have videos circulating showing their games crashing while streaming live. Though their issues aren't likely as severe as some users realizing their consoles have been bricked. Some are hoping that after a cooldown period, everything will once again be copacetic, while others are having to find repair alternatives, including various cleaning methods or liquid metal replacement.

THE PS5 BLACKOUT HAS STARTED. I called it back in early August. First came error reports and sudden shutdowns. Now we’re seeing graphics artifacts live on stream and reports of consoles dying. GTA 6 is the toughest real-world PS5 stress test I’ve seen. In the clip, I’m standing… https://t.co/WDj0CYcAm9 pic.twitter.com/mtL09rAUmH

Some Redditors have noted that these reports are lacking the context of the system's placement. User u/ChrisWolf14 , in response to a Redditor's post concerning the issue, shares that they would like people experiencing this issue to "provide more information about how they stored their console." Having consoles in spaces where warm air is trapped could lead to overheating issues with more resource-intensive games like GTA 6 . For those worried about this calamity potentially befalling their console, consider taking preventative measures. Ensure that your console is cleaned and positioned in a way that it can remain in open, cool air while playing.

With GTA 6 taking the world by storm, players are hard at work exploring Leonida and uncovering its many secrets and adventures. Notably, players have noticed that while the game continues many GTA traditions, it lacks the feature of mission replayability to the dismay of some. In other news, analysts have determined that GTA 6 runs better on the Xbox Series X than the base PS5 . The PS5 version seems to suffer from more frame rate drops than its Microsoft counterpart. However, PS5 Pro users don't really have to worry about this issue.

If you're knee-deep in GTA 6 , more news and surprises are likely to be surfaced in the coming days. Perhaps you'll cross paths with the devil throughout your travels. Either way, be sure to take care of your consoles and keep them in good working order through proper storage and cleaning and maintenance, especially while you have GTA 6 on board.

Accepting the inevitable, the elder statesmen of anthem rock took their halftime spin on stage at Netflix and the NFL ’s first ever Thanksgiving Eve game to go full bread and circuses. Under those criteria, in their first time headlining on Netflix, the Irish rockers succeeded.

Veering towards the tried and true, Bono, guitarist The Edge, bassiest Adam Clayton and drummer Larry Mullin Jr thundered through their Boomer classics of ‘Sunday Bloody Sunday’ The Joshua Tree’s ‘The Streets Have No Name’ and MLK tribute ‘Pride (In The Name of Love)’. Add to that a sprinkle of Motown’s ‘Stop in the Name of Love’ and some glorious vocals thrown in from singers and an on-field marching band and you had a party. In a nod to their latest release and the times we live in, the second song in the set was the ‘Torn’ duet with t Dolly Parton

With the obvious exception of the inclusion of the late great Dolly, who was displayed on curtains that came down from the stadium roof, it was a set that could have come almost anytime the last 25 years.

As well, it was a set that tried to turn the other cheek to the nostalgia of it all. In many ways, Bono’s vow not to use backing tracks and the pre-halftime shot that Netflix showed of U2 heading through Sofi’s catacombs on gold carts sorta told you all you needed to know.

To their credit, unlike most Super Bowl halftime shows of the past dozen years, (and expected for Jay-Z ’s Super Bowl LXI set on February 14 at Sofi), a relatively stripped down U2 didn’t bring put any super star guests Wednesday for the L.A. crowd. Walking out on the field to a chorus, the band took the in the round stage with a “thank you for having us.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Oddly ending a bit too quick to go to an ad, tonight’s shindig came halfway through the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve match with the Rams battling it out with Packers at the L.A. team’s always camera-ready stadium. A clear belt notch in the league’s desire to dramatically expand the incredibly lucrative football franchise, tonight’s much hyped game between the Packers and the Rams was given all the gloss by the Ted Sarandos and Greg Peter-run streamer of a playoff clash or the Super Bowl itself.

Having already played a few warm-up gigs, like opening the November 14 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame ceremony, during the extensive promotional tour this month for their recently released Carnaval De Luz album, tonight additionally gave U2 a chance to stretch their legs and chops for fans old and new. Aided by a stage that was rolled out and set up in less than 8-minutes, s 52-foot telescopic camera crane and a specialty camera coming down from the Sofi roof, U2’s Jesse Collins Entertainment produced set had a very 2026 professional shine.

For a big gesture band never shy to take the big stages in a big way, Netflix’s global reach can’t help U2 hawk a few more tickets for their upcoming Greatest Show on Earth tour with the best promo reel Netflix can buy. The tour begins in Mexico City in February. After shows in South America and Europe, the band and their unofficial 50 th anniversary tour ends up in North America for a 15-stadium run starting in Miami on August 13.

At the same time, as the Rolling Stones, Bruce Springsteen and many other stadium-playing legacy acts will tell you, the role of old bands is to play the old hits - - no matter how good or bad the latest album is. Bono, the Edge, Mullin and Clayton knew that back in 2002 when they played Super Bowl XXXVI in the aftermath of the 9/11 terror attacks. Using their Elevation Tour set at NOLA’s Superdome, U2 in less than 20-minutes whipped off ‘Beautiful Day,’ ‘MLK’ and ‘Where The Streets Have No Name’ and paid tribute to those who lost their lives that horrible day in NYC.

One of the biggest bands in the world for 40 years, U2 haven’t toured since 2019 and they had a little bit to prove tonight, as they made clear.

Yet, the GameDay halftime show wasn’t their first time on stage this decade.

A 40-show stint at Vegas’ Sphere starting in September 2023 saw the band pulling it off Zoo TV style, even with an injured Mullin sitting it out. The now all healed up drummer was in the Sin City crowd a couple of nights. Still, a big live draw since the mid-1980s no matter how their records charted, the Irving and Jeffrey Azoff' managed U2 are leaving no opportunity unexplored this year in a hope to return to relevance.

Leaving no marketing stone unturned, even Sofi itself got in on the act Wednesday.

articles.title: Microdrama Revenue to Hit $20 Billion in 2026, but Profits Outside China Remain Thin, Media Partners Asia Report Finds
articles.summary: Global microdrama revenue will climb 24% to $20 billion in 2026, but outside China the business has yet to prove it can make reliable money, according to new research from Media Partners Asia. The Asia-focused research and advisory firm's second annual study of the sector, "The Microdrama Economy 2026," projects the market will reach $32 […]
articles.content:
Global microdrama revenue will climb 24% to $20 billion in 2026, but outside China the business has yet to prove it can make reliable money, according to new research from Media Partners Asia .

The Asia-focused research and advisory firm's second annual study of the sector, "The Microdrama Economy 2026," projects the market will reach $32 billion by 2031, on annual growth of 9.8%. MPA's figures measure spending by viewers, advertisers and brands before app stores and payment processors take their cut. Outside China, they count only dedicated microdrama apps and their web storefronts, not general social media feeds. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'God of War' Live-Action Series: Deborah Ann Woll to Reprise Faye Role From Video Games 'Terminal List' Prequel Series 'Cry Havoc' in Development at Amazon

China still dominates. The country will generate $15.2 billion this year, or 76% of the global total, after revenue jumped 90% in 2025. MPA expects growth there to cool to 6.7% annually as viewing levels off, taking Chinese revenue to $21 billion by 2031. The firm's China figure is narrower than the National Radio and Television Administration's RMB100 billion ($15 billion) estimate for 2025, which also counts producer outlays on AI models and platform investment.

Free, ad-supported viewing overtook paid viewing in China in 2025. Advertising will make up 69% of the country's microdrama revenue this year and 79% by 2031. ByteDance , which operates Hongguo and Douyin, takes 56% of Chinese revenue, and ByteDance, Tencent and Kuaishou together command 82%.

Dedicated apps outside China will earn $4.87 billion in 2026, a third more than last year, with MPA forecasting $11 billion by 2031 on annual growth of 17.7%. The U.S. remains the biggest single market at $1.71 billion, though that is 2% lower than in 2025. Asia-Pacific excluding China, at $1.44 billion, is set to overtake the U.S. in 2029. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

India, at $322 million, now outranks Japan and Korea as the biggest market in Asia after China. It is also the fastest-growing, with revenue more than tripling this year. Local players Kuku TV and Story TV both roughly tripled their takings, and JioStar launched its microdrama service Tadka on JioHotstar in April. India is the only big market where local platforms lead, selling cheap subscriptions that bypass app-store billing. JioStar's existing streaming audience has reduced its need to pay for new users, and the company is now turning to retention and growing ad revenue.

Revenue is concentrated. ReelShort, DramaBox–GoodShort, Kunlun and NetShort together generate 65% of the total outside China, and each is either owned or financed from China. DramaBox and GoodShort announced a merger on Oct. 31, the first such deal among the sector's top players, partly so the two would stop outbidding one another for advertising. Fox, Versant and NBCUniversal are among the U.S. media companies that have bought minority stakes in the sector, while India's and Korea's biggest local platforms are gearing up to go public.

Some homegrown companies take on the Chinese-owned apps directly, among them Korea's Vigloo and Fuji TV's FOD Short in Japan. MPA sees their edge in what the Chinese apps don't have: built-in audiences, homegrown IP and talent, and a way to bill viewers without payment cards. Japanese and Korean broadcasters, studios and telcos mostly work as producers. Across Southeast Asia, telcos have sold heavily discounted passes to build reach, though MPA said it is unclear whether these bring in new paying customers or simply shift existing ones to a cheaper channel.

TikTok sits on all sides of the market. It sells advertising to the apps, carries their series and competes with them through its free app PineDrama. In Southeast Asia, ByteDance is repeating its China playbook, building audiences with free, ad-funded apps before cashing in. MPA expects TikTok to become a major player in the U.S. and Southeast Asia alike by 2031. YouTube stays open to creators and studios, while Meta mainly serves as the place where apps find new users. Even so, MPA doesn't expect free platforms to push out the paid apps, which control the IP and the billing relationship with paying customers. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Profits are the sticking point. For each dollar of revenue generated outside China, 56 cents goes to marketing and another 18 cents to app stores and payment processors. In a typical month, just one in 12 users or so pays anything. The two largest groups each bring in more than $1 billion a year, yet DramaBox posted a 3.2% net margin in fiscal 2025. ReelShort lost $12 million in 2025 before swinging to a profit of roughly $8 million in the January-March quarter of 2026.

"Demand for microdrama is established in every major market, but outside China this is still an emerging business, and it has yet to show that it can earn a durable profit," said Vivek Couto, CEO and executive director of Media Partners Asia. "The leading apps spend more than half of their revenue to acquire viewers, and most of those viewers do not pay. Consolidation has begun, and China has already moved to free, advertising-funded viewing. The companies that endure will be those that retain their viewers, bill them directly and invest in titles worth returning to."

AI is reshaping supply far faster than demand. By MPA's count, new titles listed on non-China apps will surge from around 100,000 in 2025 to 440,000 this year, with the AI-generated share climbing from 15% to 75%. Each listing represents a single title in a single language on a single app, so a series that runs in multiple languages or across multiple apps shows up more than once. Producing a title with AI costs roughly 10% of what a Los Angeles shoot would.

Audiences have been slower to switch. Live-action titles hold most of the top 50 spots on five of the six non-China platforms MPA tracks. In China, about nine in 10 titles released in 2026 are AI-made, but they bring in just 20% of the year's revenue.

"What decides a platform's economics is how many of its titles earn back the marketing spent on them," said Myat Pan Phyu, MPA's lead analyst for microdrama and vertical video. "That favors companies with established IP, stars and audiences of their own, which is why local broadcasters, studios and telecom operators matter to the next phase."

Payments may shift the math. Apple and Google process 65% of the revenue earned outside China, though legal rulings and fresh legislation in the U.S., Japan and Korea have cleared the way for web payments. Direct billing can lift margins, although the savings depend on each market's fees and payment route. MPA expects payments made outside the app stores, including through India's UPI system, to deliver roughly half of the growth outside China in 2027.

articles.title: 'Baahubali,' 'RRR' Tech Chief C.V. Rao, New SMPTE Fellow, on Why Indian Filmmakers Shouldn't Depend on Overseas Facilities
articles.summary: C.V. Rao, who helped shape the production and post-production pipelines behind S.S. Rajamouli's "Baahubali" films and "RRR," has become the first technologist from South India to be named a Fellow of the Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE). Rao, chief technology officer at Hyderabad-based Annapurna Studios, describes the honor as one that comes […]
articles.content:
C.V. Rao , who helped shape the production and post-production pipelines behind S.S. Rajamouli 's "Baahubali" films and " RRR ," has become the first technologist from South India to be named a Fellow of the Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE).

Rao, chief technology officer at Hyderabad-based Annapurna Studios , describes the honor as one that comes with added responsibility, along with a chance to learn from senior figures across the global SMPTE community. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Melania Trump Calls for ‘Peace’ When Asked About Children in Gaza and Israel at Amazon Series Premiere Chris Pratt to Continue 'Terminal List' Story in 'Savage Son' Series for Amazon

"It also reflects the tremendous technical talent available in India," Rao tells Variety . "We have developed strong capabilities in adopting and implementing advanced filmmaking technologies, and we believe the next opportunity is to contribute more actively to innovation, technology development and international standards."

"Baahubali" brought challenges well beyond what the studio had expected. The scale of the production demanded major upgrades in grading, processing power, storage, bandwidth and technical staff. For "Baahubali 2," the team set up a dedicated peer-to-peer link between Hyderabad and Los Angeles to send large volumes of material straight to Imax. The experience also led to the launch of ANR Sound & Vision, a one-stop post facility that takes projects from data management and editing through VFX, sound, grading and final mastering.

The Dolby Cinema version of "RRR" had its roots in Las Vegas, where a Dolby Cinema demo at NAB led to talks with cinematographer K.K. Senthil Kumar, who pitched the idea to Rajamouli.

"We had to travel to Germany for the Dolby Cinema processing of 'RRR,' which raised an important question: why should Indian filmmakers depend on overseas facilities for these capabilities?" Rao says. "That experience became a major motivation for establishing Dolby Cinema processing capabilities at Annapurna Studios." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rao points out that India had skilled VFX artists and capable post houses well before either film. What Rajamouli's productions brought was a new order of scale and complexity, which pushed studios to grow their capabilities, strengthen their teams and get departments working together more closely. Both films also relied on international partners. Attempting projects of that size entirely within India 10 years earlier would have been far tougher, he says, given the gaps in specialized infrastructure, processing capacity and experience at the time.

"The most significant impact was the confidence these projects created across the industry," Rao says. "They demonstrated that Indian studios could handle increasingly complex work and encouraged greater investment in our technical ecosystem."

Rao started out as a graphic designer and 3D artist. From there he worked his way through documentary and feature editing, scanning, lab work, visual effects and color grading. That time spent across departments taught him where crews run into trouble during the shoot and in post, and at Annapurna he has used it to find weak spots in workflows and build infrastructure around what productions actually need.

"We have always believed that understanding the filmmaker's requirements is just as important as understanding the technology itself," he says.

Annapurna has put money into virtual production and one of India's largest motion-capture stages. Interest is growing, but uptake has lagged expectations. During COVID, the studio saw virtual production as a way for filmmakers to stay inside controlled environments and cut down on location work and travel. The format, though, demands heavy preparation: digital sets have to be built, and camera moves and lighting mapped out, before anyone shoots a frame.

"In our industry, approvals and shooting schedules often get finalized very late," Rao says. "Even when filmmakers are interested, there may not be enough time to prepare everything properly. Under these circumstances, conventional shooting becomes the easier option."

Motion capture is gaining ground on complex action scenes, digital characters and performance-driven VFX. Rao expects both technologies to become standard tools once more productions have hands-on experience and learn where they genuinely save time. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

On infrastructure, he maintains that Indian facilities hold their own against established international hubs and can access most of the same advanced technology. Several major Indian productions now finish large chunks of their post work at home. Where India trails is research and development. Mature markets, he says, benefit from close collaboration among studios, technology companies, research institutions and creatives, while India needs to spend more on homegrown technology and on testing new workflows.

"We strongly believe infrastructure alone cannot deliver quality," Rao says. "The knowledge, experience and creativity of the professionals behind it make the real difference."

Annapurna has also set up Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos mastering facilities. Rao finds big-budget productions increasingly sold on premium formats, while mid-budget filmmakers are still weighing whether they pay off commercially. With streaming and high-end TVs giving audiences quality viewing at home, he sees premium theatrical formats as a reason to get people back into cinemas.

"However, there needs to be better alignment between mastering capabilities and theatrical exhibition infrastructure," Rao says. As more premium-format screens open across India, he expects producers to commit to these formats earlier in their release plans.

AI is already proving useful in concept development, storyboarding, previsualization, restoration and repetitive VFX tasks, letting teams test ideas faster and automate slow work.

"However, storytelling, performances, emotional expression and final artistic decisions must remain under human creative control," he says.

He sees AI working alongside existing tools rather than replacing them. Complex digital characters driven by performance may still need precise motion capture, with AI handling supporting jobs.

Whether any of this lowers costs depends on the project. Virtual production can trim location, travel and scheduling expenses, but it requires investment in infrastructure, digital assets and prep, and without proper planning it can end up costing more. AI is getting easier for smaller filmmakers to access, yet consistent professional results still call for skilled teams, computing power and quality control.

"We believe smaller productions can benefit from shared facilities and specialized technology services rather than investing in expensive infrastructure independently," Rao says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Having overseen technical pipelines for more than 500 feature-film deliveries, Rao traces most post-production trouble back to poor planning. The most frequent error is bringing post teams in too late, when VFX, sound, grading, data management and delivery specs should ideally be on the table in pre-production. Late creative changes are the other big problem. Changes come with the territory, he acknowledges, but major revisions near delivery put artists and technicians under enormous strain.

"Teams may need to work extended hours, repeat completed tasks and rush important processes to meet deadlines," Rao says. "This creates unnecessary stress, increases costs and can sometimes compromise the quality of the final product."

For India to land complete high-end international productions, Rao wants a friendlier business climate, consistent government policy, competitive incentives and simpler approvals, along with deeper partnerships with global studios and more spending on research, training and integrated facilities.

"The opportunity is to position India not merely as a cost-effective outsourcing destination, but as a reliable creative and technical partner capable of handling complete productions to international standards," he says.

Training is part of that equation. Rao wants studios to offer structured internships and mentorship, educational institutions to rework curricula alongside working professionals, and government to back specialized training centers and research.

As an SMPTE Fellow, he plans to take part in technical discussions where India's experience can help. An industry that works across many languages and production scales, under demanding workflows, has lessons to offer in digital cinema, post-production and data management, he says. He frames the fellowship as a two-way exchange, bringing ideas from global engineers and researchers back home in return.

Looking five years out, Rao expects AI, real-time rendering, virtual production and motion capture to reshape filmmaking as they increasingly converge. Annapurna will keep upgrading its infrastructure, exploring new workflows and training teams, judging each new technology on whether it solves real production problems rather than on novelty.

"Ultimately, we believe technology investments should be driven by the value they bring to filmmaking, not simply by technological advancement itself," Rao says.

articles.title: Hulu is Being Dominated by 5 Movies from the Same $3.3B Sci-Fi Franchise - and New Instalment Is in Theaters Now
articles.summary: Courtesy of Lionsgate Movies based on the idea that the future of humanity is a bleak and dystopian prospect have always been popular pieces of escapism. Every now and then, a story of hope, rebellion and despair in this kind of landscape comes along and really grabs audiences. That is exactly what happened when a series of Young […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Movies based on the idea that the future of humanity is a bleak and dystopian prospect have always been popular pieces of escapism. Every now and then, a story of hope, rebellion and despair in this kind of landscape comes along and really grabs audiences. That is exactly what happened when a series of Young Adult novels took readers to a post-apocalyptic North America known as Panem, where a ruthless authoritarian rule ensures that suffering and conformity is paramount. Four years after the release of the first book in the trilogy, The Hunger Games was released in cinemas by Lionsgate and became the first instalment in a blockbuster movie saga that has just released its sixth movie. To coincide with that release, all five previous films in the franchise have leaped to the top of the Hulu streaming chart, occupying the streamer’s entire Top 5 at the time of writing.

The Hunger Games was originally a trilogy of novels, with the first book being followed by Catching Fire and Mockingjay . The movie trilogy was released across four movies between 2012 and 2015, when it seemed that the franchise had come to an end with all four movies scoring well in reviews from both critics and audiences, and becoming Lionsgate’s most profitable franchise ever. The story follows Katniss Everdeen – played across all four movies by Jennifer Lawrence – who takes part in a televised event called the Hunger Games in place of her younger sister. The brutal challenge sees “tributes” from each of Panem’s 12 districts fighting it out until there is only one survivor  - a YA version of Stephen King’s The Running Man meets Squid Game . Katniss inadvertently becoming a beacon of rebellion against the tyranny of the Capitol and President Coriolanus Snow.

In 2020, a decade after seemingly concluding The Hunger Games story, author Suzanne Collins returned to the franchise that made her name with a new prequel novel that changed the focus of the focus of the story to follow a young Coriolanus Snow around the time of the 10 th Hunger Games, long before he became the dictator of the original trilogy. A Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes expanded on the history of Panem and the Games, fleshing out some familiar characters while paving the way for more stories, with a movie version led by Rachel Zegler being released in 2023. In 2025, Collins released her second prequel novel, Sunrise on the Reaping , which moved the story forward 40 years to the 50 th Hunger Games, and was adapted into a new movie that is playing in cinemas now. While returning to a franchise after a decade can be a daunting prospect, the new movies have defied the odds to become the highest-rated of the franchise based on audience scores on Rotten Tomatoes, even if their box office has not matched the original trilogy.

Although Sunrise on the Reaping has received the highest audience rating of any movie in the franchise - currently sitting on a huge 94% approval score - and the entire franchise is dominating streaming, Collins reportedly has no plans for at more prequels at this time. The new movie ends with cameo appearances by original franchise stars Lawrence, Woody Harrelson, and Josh Hutcherson in a short epilogue. With the film being set 24 years before The Hunger Games , there may not be any other stories worth telling, and after such a successful run there is a strong case for leaving well enough alone and allow the franchise to live on with its popularity and quality intact.

Should this be the end of The Hunger Games , or are there more stories to be told? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 5 Dead Supervillains Who Took Forever to Come Back to Life
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics In the DC and Marvel comics universes, supervillains rarely die because of the heroes’ frequent no-killing rules. And even when these evildoers are killed, they almost always come back within a few months or years. However, some supervillains have had to wait much longer to rise from the grave to cause chaos. Whether it’s because […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In the DC and Marvel comics universes, supervillains rarely die because of the heroes’ frequent no-killing rules. And even when these evildoers are killed, they almost always come back within a few months or years. However, some supervillains have had to wait much longer to rise from the grave to cause chaos. Whether it’s because others usurped their mantles or they were generally considered forgettable D-List villains, these costumed criminals spent decades in their tombs. That made it even more shocking when they came back to life to continue torturing their heroic archenemies. It may take time, but evil will always return.

This list covers some of the longest gaps between a supervillain’s death and their reintroduction in comics. Retcons where the villain merely faked their apparent demise will also be included.

Few heroes and villains have a more hate-filled rivalry than Spider-Man and Norman Osborn's Green Goblin. And their most iconic battle resulted in the death of not just Spider-Man’s first love, but also his archenemy. After Green Goblin murdered Gwen Stacy, the Web-Head’s rage led him to confront Osborn in a final, climactic battle in 1973’s Amazing Spider-Man # 122 . In the fight, Spider-Man beat Green Goblin half to death, but he managed to return to his senses and stop the beating before he delivered the killing blow. Ironically, Green Goblin later caused his own undoing when he tried to impale Spider-Man with his remote-controlled glider. However, Spider-Man jumped out of the way, and the glider struck and killed Green Goblin instead. For 23 years, Spider-Man was seemingly free from Osborn’s schemes. However, in 1996’s Peter Parker: Spider-Man #75 , Norman Osborn was revealed to have survived his injuries and faked his death. Even worse, Osborn was exposed to have been the mastermind behind the "Clone Saga" and the faked deaths and kidnappings of Aunt May and Spider-Man’s infant daughter. It’s a return fitting for someone as evil as the Green Goblin.

Today Black Adam is recognized as one of Shazam’s archenemies and among the most powerful and morally complex anti-villains in DC Comics. However, Black Adam actually died in his very first appearance. Back when Shazam was still called Captain Marvel and owned by Fawcett Comics, Black Adam debuted in 1945’s Marvel Family #1. The original champion of the wizard Shazam spent 5,000 years lost in space before eventually returning to Earth and battling the Marvel Family. When Black Adam proved to be too much of a physical threat, Uncle Marvel tricked the villain into saying “Shazam.” Once back in his mortal form, his 5,000 years immediately caught up with Black Adam, reducing him to dust. It wouldn’t be until 32 years later that Dr. Sivana used a resurrection machine to bring Black Adam back to life in 1977’s Shazam! # 28 . Since then, Black Adam has been the Marvel Family’s strongest and most recurring adversary.

For a character who can take on any identity, pinpointing Matt Hagen Clayface’s official resurrection is hard. Hagen was the second Clayface and the first to have the mud-like body and shapeshifting powers now associated with the character. However, Clayface’s malleable body wasn’t enough to save him from the Anti-Monitor’s Shadow Demons in 1986’s Crisis on Infinite Earths #12 . Hagen wouldn’t make an official return until several multiversal reboots later with Batman: Knightwatch – Batman Day Special Edition #1 in 2021. However, Hagen’s 36-year absence from DC Comics would undergo a significant complication with the release of 2026’s Clayface: Celebrity Dirt #3 . In that comic, it’s revealed that the current Clayface, Basil Karlo, uses a fake identity. Before becoming an actor, Basil Karlo was born Matt Hagen, and he changed his name to avoid the cops. This retcon means that the Clayface that’s around since 2011 has been both Basil Karlo and Matt Hagen, making his absence from comics only 26 years. But either way, the Matt Hagen Clayface was gone for decades.

One of the oldest supervillains in DC Comics history is the vampiric Mad Monk who was the first superpowered villain that Batman had ever faced. However, the Mad Monk arrived before the Dark Knight had cemented his no-kill rule. So, in 1939’s Detective Comics #32, Batman snuck into the Mad Monk’s lair and shot the vampire with silver bullets while he slept in his coffin. But 43 years later, Batman would learn that killing a vampire is never that simple. In 1982’s Detective Comics #515, the villain returned, rebranding himself as “the Monk.” The villain became the leader of a cult called the Brotherhood and had his followers kidnap people so that he could feast on their blood. The comic also revealed that the Monk was a former plantation owner named Louis DuBois who was cursed by his former slaves and transformed into a vampire. Since his reintroduction, the Monk has only made sparse appearances, but he remains a staple of Golden Age Batman comics.

Marvel Comics’ Hangman is a lesser-known but deeply disturbing vigilante and serial killer who makes the Punisher look tame by comparison. An enemy of Werewolf by Night and Spider-Woman, Hangman would kill or imprison criminals, or people he deemed to be corrupting youth, like movie producers. This noose-and-scythe-wielding psychopath met his end in 1982’s Bizarre Adventures #31 . In that issue, Hangman was seemingly stabbed to death with his own scythe by a film critic in self-defense. It would take 44 years for this D-list villain to make his triumphant comeback in 2026’s Spider-Woman Vol. 9 #1 . There, it was revealed that Hangman had faked his death and had stayed under the radar by operating as a hired killer. However, Hangman would eventually resurface to kill all of New York’s gangsters as retribution for his estranged daughter almost getting killed in a drive-by. Hangman is one villain the rest of Marvel’s criminal underworld wished had remained buried.

Which supervillain were you most excited to see make their comeback? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the  ComicBook Forum!

articles.title: ‘Four Seasons In Java’ Review: Indonesia’s Oscar Submission Is a Gorgeous, Slow-Burning Thriller With Elements of Magical Realism
articles.summary: A gloriously executed slow burn of a suspense thriller, mixed with magical realism and other genre tropes, “Four Seasons In Java” connects the themes and concerns of Indonesian writer-director Kamila Andini’s previous films in an exhilarating and emotionally moving way. It follows a formerly incarcerated, sexually abused woman who returns to her remote Javanese village […]
articles.content:
A gloriously executed slow burn of a suspense thriller, mixed with magical realism and other genre tropes, “ Four Seasons In Java ” connects the themes and concerns of Indonesian writer-director Kamila Andini ’s previous films in an exhilarating and emotionally moving way. It follows a formerly incarcerated, sexually abused woman who returns to her remote Javanese village after 20 years and finds the men behind her ordeal still in charge. Issues of female power, self-determination and challenges to the patriarchy connect with questions about trauma, memory and what it takes to reclaim home and identity. After 2021's TIFF Platform Prize winner “Yuni,” “Java” marks the second of Andini’s films to be selected as Indonesia’s international feature Oscar submission. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories How to Watch 'Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Online: The Hit Thriller Returns for Its Final Season

When Pertiwi (a magnificent Putri Marino in the present; Shofia Shireen in flashbacks) returns to her parents’ rural home in the shadow of majestic Mount Bromo, she is far from the shy, obedient 16-year-old schoolgirl her mother remembers. No longer afraid or ashamed, she is a fighter, determined to stand up for herself and others.

In contrast, the dynamic at Pertiwi’s parents’ home has not changed: Her weak-willed, alcoholic father (Iswadi Pratama) still racks up gambling debts and her mother continues to make excuses for him. Unwelcome in the village, Pertiwi sets about assembling an alternative family from fellow outcasts and brings them to live with her in an abandoned building outside the village limits. Together with former sex worker and café operator Mak Ira (iconic Indonesian actress Christine Hakim, chewing the scenery a bit here) and village madman/high school friend Kuntet (Dwika Pradnyana), who shares her interest in electrical engineering, Pertiwi develops a catering business, patronized by her one-time boyfriend Bisma (Arya Saloka), and also works on solar generators. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It takes some time for Pertiwi to tell her loved ones about what happened to her (spoiler alert/trigger warning: she was raped), but Andini powerfully uses all the elements of cinema to indicate her severe trauma. Certain people — in particular, village headman/former teacher Fajar (Totos Rasiti) — and places trigger Pertiwi’s memories, which first return as quick, jagged images crackling with horror-movie energy and later as entire devastating scenes that she seems to be able to watch as if they were a vintage TV show. At other times, she feels as if she is being followed by a heavy-breathing monster with sharp claws that only she can see.

When Pertiwi witnesses some young village men sexually abusing deaf schoolgirl Raras (Hanna Aretha O. Ginting), she literally cracks heads and determines to shine a light on the village’s dark doings. Her activism makes her return even more of a threat to Faraj and his patron Sapto (Doni Kus Indarto), the village’s richest man, who aims to keep his clan in power in whatever unscrupulous way he can.

Andini creates many striking visual metaphors. She juxtaposes the majestic nature surrounding the village and the succor that Pertiwi draws from it (her name means Mother Nature) with the evil deeds of Sapto’s family, the village headman and the corrupt police, that take place in dimly lit interiors and darkened spaces. She also contrasts the technology and light that Pertiwi and Kuntet create with their solar energy with the run-down electric plant, long exploited by Sapto and his henchmen, and the wounds it renders in nature. The light metaphor is also cleverly extended into a deus ex machina reveal as well as a magical realist ending.

Although certain scenes many have the look of a Western, as when Pertiwi and Bismas ride through fields, flats and forests, Andini also grounds the film in Javanese culture and tradition. The second of two scenes of traditional dancing and gamelan playing led by a shaman’s family, who are also treated as outcasts by the village officials, evokes a powerful magic that becomes a form of resistance. The striking, mood-setting, percussive score by Ricky Lionardi and Bottlesmoker deserves a shout out amongst the rest of the remarkable tech package.

The chief criticism is that the film is so packed with characters and incident that some story arcs and characters seem neglected and not as well integrated into the overall narrative. This is particularly the case with Pertiwi’s reunion with her fellow ex-prisoners and a striking scene at a Jakarta club where Pertiwi reads a poem accompanied by howling punk band. This critic would welcome a mini-series about Pertiwi and her mates in Jakarta.

“Hot take: Awards prognosticators adding Colman Domingo for Michael, you really don't need to add a mid performance/bad movie. You really don't,” posted a user to X on Wednesday. articles.title: Judge Blocks FCC's Move Against ABC's Station Licenses: 'This Is Not a Close Case'
articles.summary: A judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from seeking early license renewals from ABC stations, finding that the network has faced a "campaign of retaliation" for its protected speech. The FCC ordered Disney-owned ABC in April to file renewal applications for its eight owned stations, including WABC-TV New York, KABC-TV Los Angeles and […]
articles.content:
A judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from seeking early license renewals from ABC stations, finding that the network has faced a "campaign of retaliation" for its protected speech.

The FCC ordered Disney-owned ABC in April to file renewal applications for its eight owned stations. The move came a few days after Jimmy Kimmel, the network's late night host, joked that the First Lady had "a glow like an expectant widow," which prompted President Trump to call for Kimmel's firing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories How to Watch 'Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Online: The Hit Thriller Returns for Its Final Season

In a ruling on Wednesday, Judge Loren AliKhan ruled that ABC was likely to prevail on its claim that the renewal process was forbidden by the First Amendment.

"No one doubts that the Commission may enforce the law in the manner it sees fit," the judge wrote, "But in doing so, Defendants may not retaliate against or punish Plaintiffs and other broadcast license holders for disfavored speech."

The judge noted that Trump has routinely called for ABC's licenses to be revoked in response to editorial decisions. Under Brendan Carr, Trump's appointee to chair the FCC, the agency has opened an investigation of "The View" and its candidate interviews. Carr also threatened ABC over a Kimmel monologue on September 2025, saying "We can do this the easy way or the hard way."

AliKhan found that ABC has engaged in self-censorship since the FCC actions began. "The View" has avoided candidate interviews, for fear of running afoul of the "equal time" rule, while Kimmel put an interview with Texas Senate candidate James Talarico on YouTube, rather than risk airing it on broadcast. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"This is not a close case," the judge wrote.

ABC sought an injunction blocking the early renewal process, as well as an order barring "any actions, formal or informal, to coerce or threaten Plaintiffs with sanctions in an effort to alter their exercise of editorial discretion." The judge granted the former but denied the latter, saying the request was too vague.

The FCC also sought to force ABC to post an "appropriate bond" as a condition of maintaining the injunction. The judge ordered the company to post a bond in the amount of $1.

articles.title: 'Situations' Review: Greg Vrotsos' Filmmaking Debut Is a Winning, Relatable Throwback
articles.summary: “Swingers” isn’t the kind of movie that people often talk about Hollywood not making anymore. But when a new film is worthy of being mentioned in the same sentence as that 1996 comedy, it’s a reminder of how rare such projects are these days. Directed and co-written by Greg Vrotsos, who also stars, “Situations” owes […]
articles.content:
“Swingers” isn’t the kind of movie that people often talk about Hollywood not making anymore. But when a new film is worthy of being mentioned in the same sentence as that 1996 comedy, it’s a reminder of how rare such projects are these days. Directed and co-written by Greg Vrotsos , who also stars, “ Situations ” owes as much to “High Fidelity” and the “funcomfortable” storytelling of Larry David as it does to Doug Liman and Jon Favreau’s breakthrough, but the fact that it resembles a spiritual sequel to the latter — aged up but no less neurotic, with similar geographic specificity — offers a sturdy foundation for dating insights at once familiar and fresh. In his feature filmmaking debut, Vrotsos proves tough and tender — both behind and in front of the camera — while reminding audiences how vital stories about recognizable relationship dilemmas are to our moviegoing diet. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories How to Watch 'Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Online: The Hit Thriller Returns for Its Final Season

Vrotsos plays Nick, a Los Angeles photographer whose girlfriend Jessica (Katie Parker) has recently broken up with him. The rift clearly makes little sense to him, but more egregious are the dollars she’s asking for, as Katie has itemized their shared expenses in a spreadsheet — one of many script details that feels too distressing not to have come from lived experience. Despite impish encouragement by his married best friend Paul (P.J. Byrne) to get back into the dating pool, Nick feels stuck and uncertain: Now in his forties, he knows what kind of partner he wants, but getting to know strangers with repetitive chitchat is a grind. His career, meanwhile, is flourishing, but turmoil over his unresolved relationship prevents him from committing to any of the attractive options presented by his manager Brianne (Melora Walters). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Nick agrees to go on a double date with his pal Mario, whose appetite for L.A. nightlife overshadows his own lack of interest in casual flings. But after Paul bullies him into accepting a blind date with florist Gabrielle (Fernanda Andrade), Nick begins to question if he’s moved on sufficiently from his previous relationship to seriously entertain a new one. In the meantime, Katie pops back up to reconnect with him, hinting at the possibility of a reconciliation — well, once he’s remunerated her for his share of their previous cohabitation.

Much of Vrotsos’ previous work is as a character actor on shows like “Parks and Recreation,” “Orange is the New Black” and the 2017 return of “Twin Peaks,” but he has a handsome leading-man quality, leveraged effectively in “Situations” to make the character’s sensitivity more charming than exasperating. It almost certainly helps that he directs himself from his own script (co-written with Daniel Hartigan), and he injects Nick with enough complexity to make him brainy but not pretentious, introspective but not self-obsessed. Yet while our sympathies are almost immediately aligned with the character, the film doesn’t over-indulge him, or fail to hold him accountable when he makes some thoughtless decisions.

We’re relieved for Nick, for example, when he finds temporary solace in the bed of a similarly disillusioned young woman (Fiona Dourif) who playfully shares her own horror stories after the two of them flee the site of his blind date. But the movie ensures that he eventually faces Gabbie, his ghosted companion, in a forum that’s suitably awkward and naturally comedic, but more modestly believable than the seemingly obligatory public third-act humiliations that occur in studio romcoms.

Because he’s a decade or more older than the lovelorn guys in “Swingers,” Nick is less thirsty and more thoughtful as he returns to singledom. The choice both grounds his journey and amplifies his epiphanies. Those include his realization that an ex-partner’s presumption that they'll stay friends is a sign he's being kept under glass in case of emergencies — best to move on, immediately and without prejudice.

Acting opposite Parker's slightly entitled, cucumber-cool Jessica, Vrotsos makes a meal out of that moment, inflecting it with a bit of “if I only had the presence of mind to say that in real life” wish-fulfillment while digging deep into feelings as cathartic as they are painful. But he broadly and vividly portrays single living for a generation of people who grew up just too long ago to comfortably navigate a scene that mostly exists online now. More than that, they're mature enough to try and avoid petty melodrama, whether or not they succeed. That Paul — played by Byrne as a mixture of Vince Vaughn and his own buffoonish “Wolf of Wall Street” character Rugrat — is not just a married man with kids, but one who can admit to his own failures and vulnerabilities, lends forther sophistication to a story that, in less capable hands, could feel formulaic. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Despite being shot on a shoestring budget (reportedly $130K), the film looks rich and lived-in, utilizing real locations in Los Angeles’ east side in much the same way that Liman did with Hollywood’s late-‘90s watering holes. Working with cinematographer Trevor Wineman, Vrotsos favors uncomplicated setups, but repeatedly places the camera in ways that make conventional interactions more interesting. Meanwhile, composer Ben Romans finds smart, subtle ways to evoke Nick’s spartan but emotionally complex world with cues that are unobtrusive, but more intense than mere vibe-setting.

After being road-showed by distributor Utopia following a 2025 festival run, the film is due on physical media next year, but its charms feel destined for future cult adoration — again, an irony given subject matter that, in any era, has plenty of mainstream appeal. Central to its charm is the relatability of getting dumped by somebody you’d like to get back together with, not just because you still have feelings for them, but because starting a new relationship is just too much trouble. 30 years after the romantic misadventures of Favreau and his pals, this next-generation follow-up reiterates the adage that there’s someone out there for everybody, but adds an important footnote born of a single fortysomething's life experience: The first step to finding that person is often getting out of your own way. Let’s hope “Situations” is Vrotsos’ first cinematic lesson of many.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Fans have long been waiting for Shang-Chi 2 , and finally, there seems to be some movement. Although there is plenty of excitement about Avengers: Doomsday , releasing in just one month, and Avengers: Secret Wars after that, MCU fans have plenty they are looking forward to and hoping for long after that. Whereas upcoming additions like X-Men and Ghost Rider are confirmed and have concrete release dates, though, other projects are less clearly formed. On that list, certainly, is Shang-Chi 2 . The first movie, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings , debuted in 2021, and for five years, fans have been wondering whether a sequel is coming and, if so, when.

There has since been plenty of chatter about a sequel, including myriad comments from Shang-Chi actor Simu Liu himself , but nothing has been officially confirmed as far as a title, release date, or anything more substantial about the movie. Finally, that seems to be changing, with American screenwriter and film producer Dave Callaham recently giving an interview in which he suggests that work on Shang-Chi 2 is, in fact, moving forward in a more concrete way. Check out his exact comments below.

Speaking on the Escape Hatch podcast, Callaham said of Shang-Chi 2 , "I am working on a Shang-Chi sequel…it's early stages, but we're getting some real movement, which is news. So, I'm really happy about that." Although this might seem like a small update, Callaham is right that this is still news. So far, it had only been suggested that a sequel was coming, but nothing was actively being worked on. Granted, with this update, there is still very little information in terms of when this movie will actually be fully in development, much less when it might be hitting theaters.

View this post on Instagram Notably, this also sets up an interesting trajectory for Shang-Chi as a character, as he is already confirmed to be returning in Doomsday in just a few weeks. Presumably, this means that Shang-Chi 2 will be set after Doomsday and Secret Wars , which really opens up the opportunities narratively for where this story could go. However, there will no doubt be fans who just want answers to the questions left at the end of Shang-Chi , in which Shang-Chi and Katy are visited by Wong and depart with him, seemingly for some new mission, and Shang-Chi's sister, Xialing, is now the leader of the Ten Rings. Hopefully, those narrative threads are eventually addressed.

In addition to this conversation, Callaham talked about how lucky they had been to find Liu, who was not only an experienced actor who is funny and has comedic timing but also has a background in Taekwondo and parkour, making him the perfect fit for Shang-Chi . With how well-suited Liu clearly is to the role, that only makes fan hopes all the higher that they will see Liu in this role in a solo movie once again in the future.

articles.title: Recasting the Original Starship Troopers for 2026
articles.summary: One of the most iconic sci-fi movies of the 1990s is without a doubt Starship Troopers, but not for the right reasons. The adaptation of Robert A. Heinlein’s classic novel, Paul Verhoeven’s 1997 film performed poorly at the box office, did not do well with critics, and left a lot of people thinking it was […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the most iconic sci-fi movies of the 1990s is without a doubt Starship Troopers , but not for the right reasons. The adaptation of Robert A. Heinlein’s classic novel, Paul Verhoeven’s 1997 film performed poorly at the box office, did not do well with critics, and left a lot of people thinking it was an endorsement of the abuse of government and military power. But over the years, the film not only became a cult classic, but people started to realize they’d completely misunderstood the film’s satire . Watch Starship Troopers today, and it feels like a very different movie.

It’s also a movie that people have wanted to see either rebooted or given a revival and it might actually happen. In 2025, it was reported that District 9 director Neill Blomkamp is set to offer a new take on Starship Troopers . Blomkamp’s project isn’t exactly going to be a reboot of Verhoeven’s film — the 1997 film was a very loose adaptation and Blomkamp is reportedly going to stay much closer to Heinlein’s book. But even with a new take on the classic story potentially in the works, we can’t help but wonder what Starship Troopers in any form would look like if it were being made today. So, when it comes to a 2026 take on the cast, we have some thoughts.

Played by Casper Van Dien in the 1997 film — the book version of Johnny is actually Filipino which is a huge reason that we think an updated, 2026 casting for the character should be Jacinto to restore that important element. But even if background wasn’t a consideration, Jacinto would be a fantastic choice for the character. The actor has displayed an incredible range in his career, with roles spanning characters like Jason Mendoza in The Good Place and, of course, his darker turn as Mae’s Sith master the Stranger (and his disguise as smuggler Qimir) in the criminally underrated Star Wars: The Acolyte .

One could argue that Jacinto might be a little too old for the character, as Johnny starts out the story as 18, but we think it could still work with the right storytelling. Jacinto’s charm and athleticism as well as his acting skills are enough that it just feels like too strong a casting choice to skip.

Played by Denise Richards in the film, Carmen is a friend of Johnny Rico’s. She is smart and ambitious and pretty independent. Johnny has a thing for her and he ends up enlisting in Federal Service to impress her. The character is a bit more central in the movie than she is in the book. If we were recasting the film for 2026, our top pick for Carmen would be Isabela Merced. After seeing Merced play Hawkgirl in Superman as well as Dina in The Last of Us , there’s absolutely no doubt that she could brilliantly bring to life the more ambitious and athletic elements of Carmen’s character. She’d also be a lot of fun to watch in battle.

Age-wise, she’s a pretty decent fit for Carmen as a character, but Merced also has a maturity that would work well off of Jacinto. Honestly she might just be the best all-around recast fit for this film.

Played by Dina Meyer, Dizzy Flores is another friend of Johnny’s but while he was fixated on Carmen, Dizzy was infatuated on Johnny and joined the Mobile Infantry to stay close to him. Dizzy is fiercely loyal in the film, a true ride-or-die figure when it comes to Johnny. She also has a pretty no-nonsense personality and Thatcher would be a perfect choice to bring that to life in a new take on the story.

We’ve already seen how intense and tough Thatcher can be with her role as teen Natalie in Yellowjackets and it makes her perfect for a soldier character like Dizzy. We have also seen her range and the nuance she brings to her characters, which is exactly what a character like Dizzy needs. Yes, she is very much the quintessential soldier in a lot of ways, but there’s an intensity to her that Thatcher would absolutely crush.

Played by Neil Patrick Harris in the 1997 film, Carl Jenkins is a good friend of Carmen, Dizzy, and Johnny and has known them for quite some time. He’s highly intelligent and extremely observant who becomes a military intelligence officer. However, over the course of the story he becomes more secretive, a bit more sinister, and much more detached which puts strain on his friendships.

There are actually quite a few actors that could pull Carl off, but our pick is Cooper Hoffman. The actor has the right balance of smart and observant and enough range that will make watching him grow a little harder and a bit darker all the more satisfying. He is also a good balance between the physicality of some of the other characters and the intensity of some of the others. He’s a good fit for a character goes from smart kid to hardened military tool.

There are actually quite a few other characters who appear in Starship Troopers, but we’re not going to try to cast all of them. That said, we have some clear ideas about some of the more notably ones. Lt. Jean Rasczak, the teacher who becomes a squad leader would be brilliantly played by Josh Brolin — he just has that tough, authority element. Frank Grillo would be a great drill sergeant as Sergeant Zim. In the first film Jake Busey played infantryman Ace Levy and gave the character a specific sort of swagger and bravado with his quirky, eccentric character. It’s a role that the only person we can really see in the role is Jack Quaid. He feels like a perfect fit for The Boys alum.

Who would you cast in a new Starship Troopers ? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.
